items.label: FIGURE O.11
items.title: Lower emissions from poverty alleviation projected with energy efficiency and decarbonization
items.content: The figure consists of two line charts showing projected CO2e emissions relative to 2019 levels under three scenarios: Baseline (blue), Energy efficient (yellow), and Decarbonizing (red). Panel a shows projections for poverty at $2.15, and panel b shows projections for poverty at $6.85. Both charts have the x-axis representing years from 2022 to 2050 and the y-axis representing 'Relative to global 2019 CO2e emissions (%)' ranging from 0 to 50. In both panels, the Baseline scenario shows the highest emissions, followed by Energy efficient, with Decarbonizing showing the lowest emissions. Source: Wollburg, Hallegatte, and Mahler 2023. Note: CO2e = carbon dioxide equivalent. The figure shows additional emissions relative to 2019 if poverty were to be alleviated at the $2.15 and $6.85 per person per day poverty lines (expressed in 2017 purchasing power parity dollars). The baseline scenario uses historical emission intensities. Energy-efficient and decarbonizing scenarios assume that all countries achieve the top 10 percent historical performance in energy efficiency and decarbonization.
